### WHAT I READ
- the item, in full: `items/def-regular-and-t3-spaces.md`
- dependencies opened on disk: `def-topological-space`, `def-t0-and-t1-spaces`, `def-hausdorff-space`, `def-neighbourhood-top`, `def-standard-topologies` (all five declared in `deps:` and all five actually cited in the body)
- also opened to check remark claims against the corpus: `def-normal-and-t4-spaces`, `rem-separation-axiom-conventions`, `lem-regularity-via-closed-neighbourhoods`, `def-urysohn-space`, `lem-urysohn-sits-between-hausdorff-and-regular-plus-t1`, `lem-ordinal-order-topology-is-t3`, `ex-sierpinski-space-is-t0-normal-and-not-regular`, `ex-the-cofinite-topology-in-the-separation-hierarchy`, `ex-the-discrete-and-indiscrete-extremes-of-the-hierarchy`, `def-completely-normal-and-perfectly-normal-spaces`, the page manifests `library/topology/separation-axioms.md` and `library/topology/separation-axioms-examples.md`, and `research/audit/wave5-alpha.md` for the wave-5 disposition record of this item

### FINDING 1 — FATAL — location: Definition section, closing sentence ("Regularity alone implies no other separation axiom")
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "It is the *conjunction* $T_3$ that sits above Hausdorff in the hierarchy, and the proof of that is two items below."

WHY IT FAILS: On the page `separation-axioms` (`library/topology/separation-axioms.md`, `items:` array), `def-regular-and-t3-spaces` sits at position 5. Position +1 is `lem-regularity-via-closed-neighbourhoods`, position +2 ("two items below") is `def-urysohn-space` — a **definition**, which contains no proof that $T_3$ implies Hausdorff. The actual proof is in `lem-urysohn-sits-between-hausdorff-and-regular-plus-t1` (claims 1 and 3: Urysohn ⟹ Hausdorff, and regular+$T_1$ ⟹ Urysohn), which sits at position +3, three items below, not two.

This is not a stylistic slip: the same page uses "N items below" as a precise raw positional pointer elsewhere, and gets it right both times I checked it — `def-normal-and-t4-spaces` ("the theorem two items below is where [the $T_1$ hypothesis] is spent") correctly points +2 to `thm-t4-implies-t3`, and `def-completely-normal-and-perfectly-normal-spaces` ("proved two items below") correctly points +2 to `thm-perfectly-normal-implies-completely-normal`. So the convention is established and accurate elsewhere on this exact page; `def-regular-and-t3-spaces` alone gets the count wrong by one, sending a reader chasing the claimed proof of "T3 ⟹ Hausdorff" to a bare definition that doesn't contain it.

This is the same defect species Alpha already found and repaired once in this very item: the wave-5 record (`research/audit/wave5-alpha.md`, adjudication #2) confirms fatal an earlier remark in this file that misstated how many false statements the page carries and what they settle. This second instance — a false claim about *where* a proof sits — is the identical failure mode ("a Remark asserting … where something sits in the reading order") that this audit's own brief flags as the dominant source of confirmed fatal defects in this corpus, and it survived the repair pass that fixed the first instance.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Change "two items below" to "three items below," or drop the specific count and write "the theorem below" / cite `[[lem-urysohn-sits-between-hausdorff-and-regular-plus-t1]]` directly.

### ASSESSMENT
The mathematical content of the definition itself is correct: the regularity condition, the $T_3$ = regular + $T_1$ convention fork (matched against Kelley/Willard/Engelking vs. Munkres, consistent with the sibling item and the page-level `rem-separation-axiom-conventions`), the $C=\varnothing$ triviality check, the indiscrete-topology witness that regularity implies no other axiom, and the cofinite-topology witness that $T_1$ does not imply regularity are all correct and, where checked against companion witness items (`ex-sierpinski-space-is-t0-normal-and-not-regular`, `ex-the-cofinite-topology-in-the-separation-hierarchy`, `ex-the-discrete-and-indiscrete-extremes-of-the-hierarchy`), accurately supported on disk. All five declared dependencies are cited faithfully with no widened domain, hypothesis, or direction. The two forward cross-page links (`def-normal-and-t4-spaces`, `rem-separation-axiom-conventions`) say exactly what those targets say. The one fatal defect the wave-5 refuter caught in this item (the false "two false statements … make that precise" claim) has been correctly removed and replaced with text that now agrees with its sibling item. But a second, structurally identical false locational claim remains on disk, uncaught by that repair.

1 fatal, 0 nonfatal
